summary: In Greek mythology, Stratius (Ancient Greek Στράτιος), also Stratichus in Apollodorus, was a son of Nestor of Pylos. Homer names him among the brothers who gather for the dawn sacrifice to Athena when Telemachus visits sandy Pylos — a household prince rather than a Trojan-War captain.
etymology: Stratius / Stratios (Στράτιος) means "of an army"; Apollodorus' Stratichus is the same Pyliad son under a variant spelling.

sections.heading: Son of Nestor
paragraphs: In Odyssey 3 Stratius stands with Nestor's other sons when the horseman of Gerenia takes the sceptre and bids them prepare the sacrifice for Athena before Telemachus journeys on to Sparta. He has no independent aristeia in Homer; his role is dynastic presence at Pylos beside Peisistratus, Thrasymedes, and the rest of the house.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This node (stratius-nestor) is Nestor's son. Distinct from Stratius son of Clymenus of Orchomenus; from the Odyssean comrade Tzetzes has Polyphemus devour in Sicily; and from the Zacynthian suitor of Penelope (stratius-zacynthus) in Apollodorus' island catalogue.
